answer: An admission auction sells 100 entry slots per epoch at a 50 POA reserve, paid as a bond unlocked by honest work. Like a harbor admitting only ships that pay to dock, it admits bids clearing the reserve. A farm wanting 100 fake identities pays 100 x 50 = 5,000 POA, with the price climbing toward its zenith as bidders compete. One honest agent pays one bond and earns it back in fees; a plume of fake identities costs the farm money with no refund.
